summary: This program builds a small library of Book objects in a List, then collects each book's genre into a Set so that repeated genres appear only once, and prints the resulting genre list.

lines.text: Set is the interface for a collection that refuses duplicate elements, which is exactly the guarantee we want for a list of genres.
HashSet is the concrete implementation of Set we will actually create; it stores elements in a hash table, so membership checks are fast but order is not preserved.
The books themselves still belong in a List, because a library can legitimately hold two copies of the same title and the order matters.
This is the second of three Fantasy books, and those repeats are what the Set is here to collapse.
Declaring the variable as Set but constructing a HashSet is the usual Java style: the code depends only on the interface, so the implementation could be swapped later.
The enhanced for loop walks through every Book in the list, binding each one to the variable book in turn.
Adding a genre that is already present simply does nothing, so "Fantasy" ends up stored once even though three books carry it.
The \n escape sequence inserts a blank line before the heading, which separates this section from anything printed earlier.
A Set can be iterated just like a List, but the order you see is decided by the hash table and is not the order the genres were added.
